chunks: The bosom of the wise is the safe of his secrets; cheerfulness is the bond of friendship; effective forbearance is the grave of short-comings.
ai.seo_question: What are the three key virtues of wisdom, friendship, and forbearance according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this concise wisdom from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs vivid metaphors to define the psychological and social dimensions of the rational person (al-'Aql). By likening the heart to a chest for secrets and forbearance to a grave for faults, he emphasizes the internal discipline required for social harmony, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on *hilm* (forbearance) and *sirr* (secrecy). This triad highlights how inner restraint directly cultivates external communal bonds, reflecting the Imam's holistic view of character formation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 6. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
The bosom of the wise is the safe of his secrets; cheerfulness is the bond of friendship; effective forbearance is the grave of short-comings.
